ruleName: Ball Lost or Out of Bounds: Stroke-and-Distance Relief Must Be Taken
imagePrompt: Create a polished, modern semi-realistic illustration (about 75% realistic, 25% stylised) in the established junior golf quiz style. Show the edge of a golf course with rough grass transitioning to longer, wild grass behind a clear white out of bounds stake. Place a golf ball on the in-bounds side, close to but not touching the white stake. Include a golfer on the course side looking at the ball and stake. Do not include text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles.
imageAlt: A golfer observes a golf ball lying just in bounds next to a white out of bounds stake at the edge of a golf course.

sceneSpec.setting: Edge of a golf course boundary line, with rough grass on the course side and longer grass or natural area beyond.
sceneSpec.players: One golfer standing on the course side, observing a white stake positioned along the boundary.
sceneSpec.ballPosition: A golf ball resting in bounds, close to but not touching the base of a white out of bounds stake.
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: The golfer visually checking the position of the white stake and the ball relative to the out of bounds line.
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Clear identification of the position and status of an out of bounds stake and how it relates to the rules.
mustShow: White out of bounds stake firmly planted along the course boundary
Golf ball sitting on the grass in bounds, very close to the stake
mustNotShow: Any text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles

questions.title: Are White Out of Bounds Posts Out of Bounds Too?
questions.question: When you see white posts that show 'out of bounds,' is the post itself out of bounds?

choices.text: No, the post is out of bounds.
Only if a special rule says so.
Only if people running the game say so.

questions.explanation: White posts that show where 'out of bounds' starts are not part of the course. The post itself is out of bounds.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A place you are not allowed to play from. It is usually shown with white posts.
A stick or marker in the ground. Here, it means a white one that shows 'out of bounds'.

questions.teachingTip: Show kids a real out of bounds post and explain you can't play from that spot or touch it when dropping a ball.
likelyMisconceptions: Some kids may think the post is still on the course because it touches the ground.
Some may think you can lean on it or touch it for a drop.

questions.title: Are White Stakes Themselves Out of Bounds?
questions.question: White stakes define out of bounds. Is the stake itself in bounds?

choices.text: No, the stake itself is out of bounds.
Only if a Local Rule says so.
Only if the committee marks it as such.

questions.explanation: The boundary edge of the course is defined by the course-side points of the white stakes at ground level. The stakes themselves are out of bounds.
